prompt: An 11-person startup sells route-optimization software to independent pharmacies that run same-day prescription delivery. Eighteen pharmacies completed a ten-week paid pilot at $500 per month; twelve renewed and six did not. Pharmacy technicians use the product, owners approve purchases, patients receive deliveries, and outside courier services perform most routes. On-time delivery improved from 86% to 95% at renewed sites. Pharmacies above 2,500 monthly deliveries create 60% of compute and support cost but pay the same price as smaller sites. A regional wholesaler offers access to 600 pharmacies for a 25% revenue share, two-year exclusivity, and a custom integration. Separately, the CTO proposes building courier dispatch in-house for $600,000 over six months; the current partner API costs $0.40 per delivery and offers an SLA. Give the founders a 90-day pricing, sales/channel, and make-or-partner decision plan.
